memory_candidates.content: When adding a new gate to a shared verification aggregator (like verify-deploy.sh) that inspects arbitrary repo/filesystem state rather than only the deploy tree itself, check whether any test harness under scripts/tests/ spins up a bare, never-onboarded scratch git repo to exercise the deploy engine. Such a harness can silently start failing the new gate for reasons unrelated to what it's actually testing (e.g. a gate asserting .gitignore coverage of ephemeral runtime files will correctly fail a bare `git init` scratch repo with no .gitignore at all). The fix is to seed the same onboarding fixture (e.g. the documented Consumer Repo Setup .gitignore block) into the harness's scratch TARGET before its first commit -- never to relax the new gate. Discovered while wiring check-runtime-file-tracking.sh into verify-deploy.sh as gate14: two harnesses (test-deploy-propagation.sh, test-deploy-orphans.sh) both needed this fix.

For CI running a repo whose gitignored deploy tree (.claude/) must be materialized before any gate can run, and where the deploy engine drives headless nvim: probe whether the deploy/verify engine's Lua code actually needs a full lazy.nvim plugin bootstrap before assuming it does. If the engine's require() chain has no plugin dependency, add an opt-in --minimal-init DIR flag to both the deploy and verify scripts (`nvim --headless --clean --cmd "set rtp+=DIR"` instead of plain `nvim --headless`), default OFF so unset behavior stays byte-for-byte unchanged, and thread the flag from the deploy script into its own inline verify call. This avoids a plugin-clone network dependency in CI entirely. Confirmed by probing manager.load/resync_all/verify_all/find_orphans individually under --clean before wiring the flag into production scripts.
